::: {.remark .notes}

The proof needs measure theory beyond these notes.
The standard example is the
[Cantor distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cantor_distribution),
which puts no probability on any single point,
but puts all of its probability on a set of total length 0,
so any candidate density would integrate to 0 over a set of probability 1.

Every continuous random variable in these notes also has a
[probability density function](#def-pdf).
Continuous random variables without a density
do not arise in applications.

:::
